title: KPI Harpoon: provenance harmonizer and telemetry gateway for inference metrics
creator: Ana Patel
description: Build a lightweight telemetry gateway (internal codename: KPI Harpoon) that normalizes inbound Prometheus and OTLP metrics for inference traffic, attaches deterministic provenance headers, applies a small set of adaptive label reshaping rules, and emits stable KPI envelopes for downstream SLO pipelines. This ticket covers the gateway prototype, unit + integration tests, a canary rollout plan, and initial dashboard wiring for latency/error dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype gateway accepts OTLP/Prom scrape payloads and emits a canonical KPI envelope to the metric bus
Gateway attaches a deterministic provenance token (trace-anchor) derived from request attributes and trace/span IDs for downstream correlation
Label reshaping rules reduce high-cardinality model/route labels by >90% in synthetic load test without losing per-model SLO signal
End-to-end test: a traced request ingested through the gateway appears in Trace UI linked with KPI in latency dashboard within 30s
Canary rollout plan documented and smoke-tests automated in CI
implementation_steps: Design gateway API: scrape endpoint, OTLP receiver, and lightweight HTTP ingest for edge producers
Implement provenance token (trace-anchor) algorithm using trace/span + deterministic hashing of model_id + route (configurable salt)
Add rule engine for label reshaping: prefix-whitelist, numeric bucketing, consistent-hash model aliasing
Integrate with existing metric bus (kafka/ingest topic) and emit canonical envelopes with metadata schema v1
Create unit tests for provenance derivation and property-based tests for cardinality reduction guarantees
End-to-end integration test: local harness that runs a small inference runtime, emits OTLP/Prom metrics, and validates KPI envelope in downstream consumer
Add feature flagging and rate-limited canary rollout with traffic shadowing and metrics comparison job
Wire up basic dashboard panels (latency/error by provenance token, model-group) and a smoke alert
notes: We intentionally avoid re-writing customer-provided labels; reshaping is additive and produces a canonical label set alongside original labels for debugging
Provenance token must be stable across retries to allow accurate aggregation; we derive from trace ID + immutable request attributes
Tradeoff: aggressive label canonicalization reduces cost but can hide rare model regressions; introduce a sampling path that preserves full labels for 0.1% of traffic
We will keep the gateway stateless; all shaping decisions are deterministic so multiple replicas are safe behind a load balancer
Fallback: if OTLP payload cannot be parsed, gateway forwards raw payload to dead-letter topic with attached error code for analysis
risks: Incorrect provenance derivation could break downstream attribution; mitigate with canary checks and reconciliation job
High write amplification if canonical envelopes are duplicated across downstream topics; monitor throughput and apply batching
Potential on-path latency for edge producers; we will measure p95 add-on and provide an asynchronous fire-and-forget ingest mode
test_plan: Unit tests for token derivation and label rules
Property-based tests for cardinality reduction across synthetic model_id distributions
Integration: end-to-end harness with traced requests and assertion of KPI linkage in dashboard
Load test: 100k requests/min synthetic to validate CPU/memory and backpressure behavior
Canary: run gateway for 1% of production traffic for 48h and compare SLO deltas against baseline
rollout_plan: Deploy to staging and run smoke test suite
Canary on 1% production traffic with shadowing to avoid double counting
If canary passes, increase to 10% for 24h and run reconciliation checks
Full rollout with monitoring runbook and rollback playbook
